subject: Production: SDK stream parser causing elevated 5xxs and p99 latency
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@streamline-commerce.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T15:24:00Z
Subject: Production incident: client 1.4 roll caused 5xx spikes and streaming stalls

Hi Olga / Rishi,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 502/504 and streamer stalls after rolling Streamline's mobile client to SDK v1.4.0 this morning at 08:10 PT. P99 latency for our checkout streaming endpoint jumped from ~210ms to >2.3s and error-rate climbed from 0.2% to 7.6%.

Key symptoms: 
- Long lived streams getting reset mid-response (client-side reconnects).
- Intermittent header parsing errors surfaced in our edge proxy logs: "incomplete header block" and "trailer association mismatch".
- Reproduces consistently when using the latest SDK with streaming coalescing enabled; rolling back the client to SDK v1.3.2 reduces errors to baseline.

I attached a short trace (sdk_error_trace.txt) and a minimal repro app. This is in production (US-West) and impacting checkout flows for ~12% of requests. We need an urgent mitigation and ETA for a patch.

Can you confirm whether this matches anything in Redwood's release notes or known parser regressions? We can be on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform
Streamline Commerce

Attachments: sdk_error_trace.txt, repro-instructions.txt

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production incident: initial triage notes

Alex / Olga — quick triage from the runtime side after looking at the trace-snippet you attached. Summary below; I'll follow up with a proposed patch.

What we see (high level):
- The client v1.4.0 introduced an optimization that coalesces small chunked frames and emits a combined header/trailer pair to reduce syscall overhead.
- On several connection samples, our server's streaming parser is associating the combined trailer with the wrong request when there are back-to-back small payloads behind a proxy that does header-affine pooling. That leads to an internal parse error and an immediate connection reset from the runtime (manifesting as 502/504 at the edge).
- This is triggered only when: streaming coalescing = enabled (client), and the upstream proxy performs connection multiplexing with a short keep-alive window.

Immediate mitigation options (pick one):
1) Customer-side rollback to SDK v1.3.2 (you reported this works).
2) Server-side temporary mitigation: disable streaming coalescing merge path on the load path for the affected region (adds some CPU overhead but preserves correctness). I can flip this per-tenant in ~12 minutes.
3) Quick client patch (v1.4.1) to avoid emitting combined header/trailer sequences for now; estimated PR + release in ~3 hours.

I'll open ENG-8123 and attach the trace (trace-snippet.log). If you want the fastest fix with minimal risk, option 2 (server toggle) is the way to go and can be done without a customer deploy. If you prefer us to ship a client fix, we'll prioritize it immediately.

I'll prepare a short reproducer and ETA for the patch.

—Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: trace-snippet.log

Hannah — escalating for visibility. Streamline (important customer, SC-4821) saw a production regression after rolling an SDK which triggers a parser edge-case in our streaming runtime. They rolled back and are requesting an ETA and credits.

Summary: 
- User impact: increased 5xx rate and p99 latency for checkout streaming (US-West); customer rolled back to SDK v1.3.2, which restored baseline.
- Root cause (triage): client-side streaming coalescing + upstream proxy pooling can cause trailer/header association issues in the runtime parser.
- Immediate mitigations: server-side toggle to disable coalescing merge path (low-risk, reversible) OR client patch (v1.4.1) in ~3h. Rishi recommends the toggle for fastest correction.

Request: can you review for exec-level approval of the credit and a short note to the customer? I'll stand up the server toggle once we have alignment.

—Olga
